project: Wuxia Life P11 Stage-Route-Driven Narrative Scheduling
description: Turn stageConfig and routeDefinitions from readable narrative config into real runtime scheduling inputs by adding shared stage and route signal detection, wiring stage-aware and route-aware priority logic into the event scheduling flow, attaching minimal wuxia content metadata and validation content packs, and proving the behavior through a dedicated P11 scheduling gate and closure report without expanding into a second world pack or a large strategy rewrite.

userStories.title: Generate stage expectation baseline report
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a baseline report of stage expectations versus actual signals so that P11 starts from measured scheduling gaps instead of assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Produce a report for ages 0-10, 10-20, 20-30, and 30-40 using current simulation output
For each stage, list expected signals from stageConfig.feedbackExpectation.expectedSignals
For each stage, list actual signals observed in records, grouped by signal type
Save the report under docs/test-reports/
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Classify stage coverage gaps
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want stage baseline gaps classified by cause so that later P11 stories target real scheduling failures instead of content guesses.
acceptanceCriteria: Classify each missing stage signal as no-content, weak-scheduling, or weak-detection
Record at least one example for each classification that appears in the baseline report
Keep the output in docs/test-reports/ as a follow-up note or appended section
Do not modify scheduling logic in this story
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Generate route scheduling baseline audit
userStories.description: As a designer, I want a route-level audit of reinforcement and divergence coverage so that I can see where route definitions are not yet affecting the runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: For each primary wuxia route used in P8 personas, report configured entry, reinforcement, divergence, and identity points
For each route point, report whether simulation records show a matching event, flag, or summary signal
Identify which route points are configured but never scheduled
Save the route audit under docs/test-reports/
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Define normalized stage and route signal vocabulary
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one shared vocabulary for narrative signals so that scheduler logic and reports stop inventing parallel names for the same stage and route outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Define normalized signal keys for stage expectations such as origin, route_entry, relationship_shift, achievement, and age40_identity
Define normalized signal keys for route reinforcement, divergence, and identity coverage
Document the signal vocabulary in code comments or a small design note near the implementation
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement shared signal detection helpers
userStories.description: As a developer, I want stable signal detection helpers so that runtime scheduling and reports evaluate stage and route coverage through one shared ruleset.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a shared helper that maps simulation records and state to the normalized signal vocabulary
The helper supports stage expectation checks for all four 0-40 age bands
The helper supports route point checks for entry, reinforcement, divergence, and identity signals
Existing reports can call the helper without duplicating parsing logic
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Wire stage feedback state into scheduling context
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the active stage and its missing expected signals available inside the scheduler so that later priority rules can use real stage state.
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduling context reads the current life stage from stageConfig
Scheduling context computes which expected stage signals are already satisfied and which remain missing
No event priority changes are introduced in this story beyond exposing the data
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add stage-aware priority bias for missing signals
userStories.description: As a player, I want low-feedback stages to bias toward missing signal types so that each life stage produces visible narrative progress instead of empty advancement.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a scheduling policy that reads the current stage and its missing expected signals before selecting candidate content
When a stage is missing one of its expected signals, scheduling increases priority for content that can supply that signal
The policy changes priority weights rather than forcing one exact event every run
Existing non-stage-gated content can still trigger when valid
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Expose route reinforcement needs in scheduling context
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the scheduler to know which configured reinforcement points are currently relevant so that route support can be driven by routeDefinitions instead of hardcoded branches.
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduling context reads routeDefinitions.reinforcementPoints for the active run
The context can identify relevant reinforcement points by age band and configured event or flag hints
No reinforcement priority change is introduced in this story beyond exposing the data
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add route reinforcement priority bias
userStories.description: As a player, I want my early route tendency to receive reinforcing content in the correct age band so that my path feels deliberately supported.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime reads configured route reinforcement points during event scheduling or prioritization
At least one reinforcement point for martial, scholar, social, wealth, and wanderer routes can affect scheduling outcome
Reinforcement scheduling uses configured age band and configured event or flag hints rather than hardcoded persona branches
Existing route identity summaries remain functional
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Expose route divergence needs in scheduling context
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the scheduler to know which configured divergence points are currently relevant so that route separation can be driven by routeDefinitions instead of persona-specific casework.
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduling context reads routeDefinitions.divergencePoints for the active run
The context can identify relevant divergence points by age band and configured event or flag hints
No divergence priority change is introduced in this story beyond exposing the data
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add route divergence priority bias
userStories.description: As a player, I want midlife route divergence to be triggered by configured route points so that different personas do not collapse into the same experience.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime reads configured route divergence points during event scheduling or prioritization
At least one configured divergence point for wealth vs wanderer and one for martial vs deviant can affect scheduling outcome
Divergence scheduling can prefer content that confirms route separation by event, flag, or summary-visible identity signal
The behavior is driven by route config, not a hardcoded persona id list
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add stage and route coverage metadata to targeted content
userStories.description: As a developer, I want targeted content items to declare which stage signal or route point they satisfy so that scheduling can prioritize them without hidden runtime maps.
acceptanceCriteria: Add metadata fields or equivalent config declarations for stage signal coverage on targeted content items
Add metadata fields or equivalent config declarations for route reinforcement or divergence coverage on targeted content items
Keep the metadata inside existing narrative config or content structures rather than creating a second parallel schema
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add first stage-gap validation content slice
userStories.description: As a designer, I want one small wuxia content slice that satisfies a 20-30 stage feedback gap so that the new stage-aware scheduler has real content to select.
acceptanceCriteria: Add or revise the minimum content needed to cover at least one 20-30 stage feedback gap
The content item declares which stage signal it satisfies
No unrelated system expansion is introduced
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add first route-divergence validation content slice
userStories.description: As a designer, I want one small wuxia content slice that satisfies a 30-40 route divergence gap so that the new route-aware scheduler has real content to separate targeted paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Add or revise the minimum content needed to cover at least one 30-40 route divergence gap
The content item declares which route divergence point it satisfies
The content remains limited to the minimum P11 validation pack
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Verify scheduler-content wiring for stage bias
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want proof that stage-aware scheduling actually changed content selection so that the validation content is not being triggered by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: Add focused diagnostics or tests showing the scheduler considered missing stage feedback when choosing targeted content
Record at least one positive example where missing stage feedback changed candidate priority
Save the verification note under docs/test-reports/

userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want proof that route-aware scheduling actually changed content selection so that divergence and reinforcement improvements are attributable to route config.
acceptanceCriteria: Add focused diagnostics or tests showing the scheduler considered route reinforcement or divergence requirements when choosing targeted content
Record at least one positive example where route-aware scheduling changed candidate priority
Save the verification note under docs/test-reports/
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add P11 scheduling gate or report command
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want a dedicated P11 scheduling gate or report so that stage-route-driven scheduling can be verified independently of the broader playability gate.
acceptanceCriteria: Add one stable command or scripted report for P11 scheduling verification
The output reports stage expectation coverage for all four age bands
The output reports route reinforcement and divergence coverage for the targeted routes
The output clearly marks pass, warning, or fail for scheduling coverage
Save machine-readable and human-readable output under stable paths
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Generate P11 regression and closure report
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a closure report comparing pre-P11 and post-P11 scheduling evidence so that the next phase starts from verified progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Run npm run gate:playability after P11 changes
Run the P11 scheduling gate or report after P11 changes
Compare before and after stage signal coverage for each age band
Compare before and after route reinforcement and divergence coverage for targeted routes
Summarize residual gaps that still require later persona strategy or second-theme work
Save the closure report under docs/test-reports/
Typecheck passes
